content: Did-you-mean options for personal-KB vocab (10k-100k terms): (1) stdlib difflib.get_close_matches - fine per-term but O(N) scan over vocab; SO benchmark: 0.58s per lookup against 15k strings - unacceptable for full-vocab scans, OK for small candidate sets; (2) SymSpell/symspellpy (port of SymSpell v6.7.2, MIT, pure Python + editdistpy fast comparer) - 0.033ms/word at edit-distance 2, needs precomputed delete-dictionary built from corpus frequencies (SIF has term frequencies via FTS5 vocab); (3) SQLite FTS5 trigram tokenizer (SQLite >= 3.34.0) - substring/fuzzy candidate generation in SQL, pairs well with difflib/rerank of small candidate set. spellfix1: NOT compiled into CPython sqlite3 (verified locally 2026-11-07 on macOS py3.13/SQLite 3.50.4: 'no such module: spellfix1') - cannot be relied on for a pip-distributed pure-Python package. Recommended SIF shape: trigram-FTS5 or first-letter/length-bucket candidate generation in SQL + difflib ranking + FTS5 term-frequency prior, all zero-dep; symspellpy only if quality insufficient. Query history suggestions: prefix match over stored query table.
